scenario.figure_or_table: Fig. 4(a) with Table I and Section II/III text (MemPool-2D baseline); compared against Fig. 4(b) MemPool-3D MoL
scenario.description: Steady-state HotSpot v7.0 thermal simulation of the baseline MemPool-2D SOC (4.8 x 4.8 mm die, 64 tiles of 425 x 425 um, 50% tile utilization, 40 W TDP) in a flip-chip package with TIM, heat spreader, heatsink, C4 bumps, substrate, solder balls, underfill and PCB. The paper reports Tmax of 46 C above ambient. The detailed 2D floorplan is only referenced to prior work [38] and is not given in this paper.
scenario.architecture: MemPool 256-core 32-bit RISC-V many-core SOC with 64 tiles (4 cores per tile, 16 KiB SPM blocks, 2 KiB I$ per tile), shared L1 SPM of 1 MiB, commercial 28 nm technology, 2D baseline
scenario.workload: Full workload at the 2D-SOC thermal design power of 40 W (larger workload baseline); the tile power breakdown is shown as percentages only (cores, I$, SPM, interconnects, others) in Fig. 3
scenario.operating_point: Steady state, ambient 27 C, results reported as temperature above ambient; Tmax,2D = 46 C; heatsink-to-ambient Rconv 0.17 K/W; PCB-to-ambient natural convection Rconv 50 K/W; 3D MemPool-3D comparison case (not selected): Tmax 55 C memory die and 57 C logic die

original_setup.solver: HotSpot v7.0 steady-state block/grid RC thermal model (finite-difference). The paper says it was validated against ANSYS and a thermal test chip. It assumes uniform power density within each block. Ambient is 27 C. (PDF pages 3-4)
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper reports no optimizer for the selected MemPool-2D baseline. It only compares four fixed tile-activity patterns P1-P4 from ref [38], which is a separate sweep and not part of this scenario.
original_setup.controller: None. No DTM or runtime controller is simulated. DTM techniques appear only as background in the introduction.
original_setup.benchmark: MemPool-2D baseline: 256-core 32-bit RISC-V many-core SOC with 64 tiles, 4 cores per tile, 16 KiB SPM blocks and 2 KiB I$ per tile, 1 MiB shared L1 SPM, commercial 28 nm. Die is 4.8 x 4.8 mm, tiles are 425 x 425 um at 50% utilization, TDP is 40 W (full workload), steady state. Source: Section II and Fig. 4(a), PDF page 3.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum on-chip temperature of the MemPool-2D die, Fig. 4(a) thermal map
thermal_observable.aggregation: Steady-state maximum over the die (Tmax, junction to ambient), HotSpot v7.0, single value for full workload at 40 W

A simplified Studio thermal stack may not reproduce this path or the 46 C result.
The 2D floorplan is not in this paper (only referenced to ref [38]). No block coordinates or per-block watts are published. Only the die size, tile size, tile count and the 40 W total are given.

The scenario is steady state only. There is no transient or power-trace data, no controller or DTM, no optimizer, and no reliability analysis in the selected scenario.
The 2D die silicon thickness and thermal conductivity, and the 2D-specific layer stack, are not tabulated. Table I lists 3D memory/logic die layers only.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only. The scenario is the MemPool-2D baseline from W4387010219: a 4.8 x 4.8 mm die, 64 tiles of 425 x 425 um, 40 W TDP, and a paper-reported steady-state Tmax of 46 C above a 27 C ambient from HotSpot v7.0. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so it is steady-state only and has no transient trace. Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false, and the input gate failed because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and both the floorplan and power_w are empty. The scientific gate also failed and nothing was independently verified. No Studio temperature exists, so comparison_valid is false and the 46 C value cannot be compared numerically with any Studio output. This is not a replication, exact or approximate. The paper's published 2D observable is the die maximum for the 40 W full workload, but its hotspot location is not stated. No pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace data, source commit, or generated-placement assumption applies here, and no input.flp or input.ptrace was produced. A future comparison would need matching location (die maximum), aggregation, steady regime, and boundary assumptions, namely the flip-chip package with a 0.17 K/W heatsink and 50 K/W PCB path. The paper's own 3D MoL results (55 C memory die, 57 C logic die) belong to a different stack and must not be mixed with this 2D baseline. Only qualitative sensitivity can be discussed: package path, power split and floorplan would all strongly affect Tmax, but their effects cannot be quantified from the available inputs.
